observations: Two large circular forms dominate the upper half: a concentric-ringed spiral on the left and a black-outlined rectangle on the right, both filled with dense overlapping lines in yellow, pink, and blue.
The lower third shifts to a row of grey and white rounded column shapes outlined in yellow and black, set against a near-black background, creating a stark tonal drop from the busy upper zone.
A white zigzag border runs along the left and top edges, and loose lettering fills the top band, all rendered in the same thick black outline style as the central forms.
reading: Two eye-like forms sit side by side — one a tight spiral, the other a cross-hatched rectangle — both ringed with spiky blue frills that suggest agitation or alertness. Below them, pale rounded columns hang into darkness, quieter in color and feel. The image holds two moods at once: the upper zone loud and compressed, the lower zone hollow and still.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #107 and nnxyz nnotb #109 show how differently the same series can land — #107 dense with saturated color across the full field, #109 stripped to two tones and open space. #108 sits between those extremes.

connections.reason: Both works place two lens-like circular forms at center surrounded by radiating lines and layered color, but #107 spreads that density across the entire field while #108 lets the lower zone go dark and sparse.

lookingQuestion: What does the shift in color density between the upper and lower halves do to how your eye moves through the image?
